title: Openness of versality for curve families
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Here a family $x$ over a scheme $U$ locally of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ is versal at a finite type point $u$ if the following lifting condition holds. For every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local rings with common residue field $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, a map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and a deformation over $A'$ of $x_u$ together with an isomorphism of its restriction with the pulled-back family over $A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism with the given deformation extending that isomorphism. Let $U$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and let $x\in\mathcal C(U)$. If $x$ is versal at a finite type point $u_0\in U$, there exists an open neighbourhood $U'\subseteq U$ of $u_0$ such that $x|_{U'}$ is versal at every finite type point of $U'$.

source.place: Tag 0D59 (lemma-curves-defo-thy), over Spec Z; artin.tex definition-versal and definition-openness-versality.

proof.text: Apply Artin's strong-effectivity route directly to $\mathcal C$. The statement of [lem-sfb-curve-descent-isom-spaces] supplies a category fibred in groupoids and represents each Isom presheaf by an algebraic space, the diagonal hypothesis of the criterion. For a ring diagram $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, put $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T'=\operatorname{Spec}B'$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then $T\to T'$ is a thickening and $T\to S$ is affine. By [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout], its scheme pushout is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B')$ (swap the two ring-product coordinates). Thus [lem-sfb-curve-infinitesimal-pushout] gives precisely the groupoid equivalence required for (RS*), with the specified gluing isomorphisms retained. Limit preservation, including descent of arrows and eventual equality, is exactly [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation].

source.place: Tag 0D59 (lemma-curves-defo-thy), through Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy); Tags 0D53, 0D55, 0D56 for the curve versions.

proof.text: Let $(R_n,x_n)$ be any system required by condition (4) of the criterion, and write $x_n=(X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n)$. Forget only the fibre-dimension bound. The families are flat, proper and finitely presented algebraic spaces, and the cartesian transition arrows are exactly the compatible isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-proper-space-square-zero-effectivity]. Every transition $R_m\to R_n$, not just consecutive ones, has square-zero kernel by the system's hypothesis. Apply that node to obtain a flat proper finitely presented $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R=\varprojlim R_n$, and compatible identifications of all its reductions with the given $X_n$.

source.place: Tag 0D3X (lemma-spaces-defo-thy), square-zero strong-effectiveness construction inside its proof.

proof.text: The object just constructed belongs to $\mathcal C$. Indeed $R\to R_1$ is surjective: successively lift an element of $R_1$ to $R_2,R_3,\ldots$ using the surjective consecutive maps. Its kernel $I$ has $I^2=0$, since in each coordinate products of two elements of $I$ lie in $(\ker(R_n\to R_1))^2=0$. Every map $R\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field kills $I$ (a square-zero element in a field is zero), hence factors through $R_1$. Associativity of base change identifies the geometric fibre $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $X_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R_1}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The latter has dimension at most one because $x_1\in\mathcal C(\operatorname{Spec}R_1)$. This covers all geometric fibres, including empty ones, and proves the bound without a dimension semicontinuity theorem. The compatible reduction isomorphisms of step 2 are arrows of $\mathcal C$ because its fibres are full groupoids of the same families. Thus condition (4) holds for $\mathcal C$, not merely for the larger proper-space groupoid.

source.place: Tag 0D59 (lemma-curves-defo-thy), the embedding equation-curves-over-proper-spaces: explicit verification that square-zero effectivity restricts to curves.

proof.text: The four hypotheses of [lem-sfb-artin-square-zero-effectivity-openness] now hold: the Isom representation, (RS*) and full limit preservation are step 1, and square-zero strong effectivity is steps 2 and 3. Its base is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, its test bases are schemes locally of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and its versality condition uses exactly the Artinian local lifting problem in the item, including extension of the specified isomorphism over $A$. Applying its conclusion to the given $U,x,u_0$ produces the required open neighbourhood $U'$ and versality at every finite type point of $U'$.
